summary.text: Whales are fully aquatic placental marine mammals that feed, mate, give birth and raise their young at sea.
Baleen whales strain krill and plankton from water with baleen plates, while toothed whales use conical teeth to catch fish or squid.
Whales evolved from land-living mammals, so they must surface regularly to breathe air through blowholes on top of their heads.

facts.label: Time underwater
facts.value: Sperm whales can stay down up to 90 minutes

facts.label: Closest relatives
facts.value: Hippopotamuses, diverged about 54 million years ago

items.prompt: A whale takes an enormous mouthful of seawater, then pushes the water out and keeps the tiny animals inside. Which feature makes this possible?

options.label: Fringe-like plates that let water out but hold food in
Rows of conical teeth that grip fish and squid
A blowhole that strains food from the water
A thick layer of fat that sieves the mouthful

items.explain: Baleen plates expel the water while retaining the krill and plankton the whale feeds on.

items.prompt: A whale drifts quietly, then rises toward the surface at regular intervals. Why must it do this?

options.label: It must dry its skin to stay warm-blooded
It must rest on shore between dives
It must take in oxygen through gills near the surface
It evolved from land mammals and must breathe air through its blowhole

items.explain: Whales evolved from land-living mammals and must regularly surface to breathe air, which they take in through blowholes.

items.prompt: A friend insists dolphins are not whales. How would a biologist who classifies by ancestry respond?

options.label: Dolphins are whales only if they are larger than 10 metres
Formally, dolphins and porpoises can be counted as whales
Dolphins and whales belong to separate orders
Only the blue whale is a true whale in any scheme

items.explain: Whale is an informal grouping of large cetaceans, but from a formal, cladistic perspective dolphins and porpoises may be considered whales.

items.prompt: Among animals outside the cetaceans, which is the closest living relative of whales?

options.label: Seals
Sharks
Hippopotamuses
Sea turtles

items.explain: Their closest non-cetacean living relatives are the hippopotamuses.

items.prompt: A species of whale that favours cold waters is spotted near the equator. What is the likeliest reason?

options.label: It migrated there to give birth
It migrated there because hunting is allowed only in warm water
It migrated there to find food that only lives near the equator
It was shedding blubber that cold water had built up

items.explain: Most species prefer colder waters and migrate to the equator to give birth.

items.prompt: A toothed whale is found to be completely blind yet healthy. What best explains its survival?

options.label: A well-developed sense of smell
Very keen hearing, above and below the water
Throat pleats that detect prey
Baleen plates that sense movement

items.explain: Toothed whales have such keen hearing, above or below the surface, that some can survive even if they are blind; the strong sense of smell belongs to baleen whales.
